The stack pushes and pops the element from the back of the underlying container, known as the top of the stack. What is a copy constructor and why do we need it?

TA: 
A copy constructor is a special member function that initializes a new object as a copy of an existing one. It's invoked when you pass an object by value, return one from a function, or explicitly create a copy. This is called a shallow copy. [1](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/copy_constructor)

[Student_Question]
How do C++ templates actually work during the compilation process?

TA: 
C++ templates are not compiled immediately when defined. Instead, they are blueprints. During compilation, when you instantiate a template with a specific type (like `std::vector<int>`), the compiler performs *template instantiation*: it generates a concrete version of that function or class by substituting the template parameter (e.g., `T`) with the actual type (`int`). This process is called *monomorphization*. [1](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/templates)
